entities.summary:
Navaratri is an annual Hindu festival observed in honor of the goddess Durga, an aspect of Adi Parashakti, the supreme goddess. It spans over nine nights, first in the month of Chaitra, and again in the month of Ashvin (September–October). The festival is observed for different reasons and celebrated differently in various parts of the Hindu Indian cultural sphere. Theoretically, there are four seasonal Navaratris, but in practice, it is the post-monsoon autumn festival called Sharada Navaratri. The festival is an essential part of Hindu culture and is a significant event in South Asian history. It has been celebrated for centuries and is an integral part of the region's cultural heritage. The festival is also a symbol of the triumph of good over evil and the victory of light over darkness.

The festival has a rich history and is mentioned in ancient Hindu scriptures such as the Mahabharata and the Puranas. It is believed to have originated in the Vedic period and has been celebrated in various forms over the centuries. The festival is observed with great enthusiasm and devotion by millions of people in India and other parts of the world. It is a time of great spiritual significance and is marked by various rituals, ceremonies, and worship of the goddess Durga.

The festival has had a significant impact on the culture and society of South Asia. It has influenced the art, literature, and music of the region and has been an important part of the region's cultural identity. The festival has also played a significant role in the social and economic lives of the people in the region. It has been a time of celebration and rejoicing for millions of people and has helped to strengthen social bonds and community ties.

As the festival continues to be celebrated with great enthusiasm and devotion, it remains an important part of South Asian history and culture. It is a symbol of the region's rich cultural heritage and a testament to the enduring power of faith and devotion.
